blocks.x: One governed decision API with replay outperforms a zoo of embedded models.

Decision hubs beat model sprawl is not a slogan; it is a delivery position. The evidence is consistent across industries — the constraint is rarely technology; it is whether the operating model takes this seriously from sprint one.

items: Separability (models score, policy decides, humans supervise) survives audit and staff turnover.
Champion-challenger discipline makes model risk a measured, improving quantity.
Decision replay converts regulatory questions from expeditions into queries.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: What is the classical baseline every proposed capability must beat, measured on identical data?
Who signs the go/no-go gate, and what evidence do they require before signing?
Show us a negative result you documented — the discipline is the product.

blocks.x: The failure mode is predictable: enthusiasm funds the demo, budget cycles gate the industrialization, and by the time the governance conversation starts, shadow usage has already created the exposure the review was meant to prevent.

items: falsifiable criteria and locked baselines before build; the demo is the least important artifact.
named owners, run models and escalation paths agreed with the operating team, not for it.
replay trails, control tests and documentation as artifacts of the build — never reconstructed.

blocks.x: p99 decision latency under 150 ms is a production standard, not an aspiration.
